ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: the council's priorities
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What the advisor watches, from the food against the winter to a promise about to break, and what its buttons do
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Start at the top of the list. Gentle advice sits low and never shows among the alerts.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Priorities, in the Colony section of the council window, lists what the colony needs right now, worst first. The advisor looks again every hour, and each piece of advice says why it matters, what helps, and a rotating tip. It never acts on its own: every button only shows, plans or opens something for you to decide on.

table.li: Show me | Goes to the people, rooms or things the advice is about.
Plan the room | Opens the room planner on the fitting room, at the size the colony needs.
Upgrade the room | Opens the planner on a room you've built: pick it, and only what's missing is planned.
Go to | Opens the council page that deals with it: Decrees for a decree or an empty office, World for a mission or a world event, Wishes for a promise, Calendar for a day.

Its own action | Some advice can do the first step for you: show the mission's quest, open the camp's letter, open the Work tab, plan wall lamps where beds lie dark, or plan chairs and lamps at a workshop's benches.
Read more | Opens the Almanac page on it.

li.heading: What it watches

table.li: Food | the food against the coming winter, spoiling food, blight, ripe crops before frost, a week without fruit or vegetables, food that won't keep through a mild winter in a tribe or a manor
Shelter and warmth | beds and barracks, cold or hot months ahead, the weather's troubles, stores left under the open sky before winter, firewood short of what the fires will burn by spring
Health | doctors, medicine and a hospital, the only doctor with nobody to tend them, convalescents back at work, a plague or a famine in the region while the colony is short of what helps
Comfort | rooms without light, beds no light reaches, meals eaten without a table, recreation and its hours, strain near breaking, loneliness, clothes worn to rags

The council | wishes about to lapse, promises about to break, trust, a decree whose reason has passed while its moods still cost, an office empty when it matters (no physician with the sick in bed, no reeve at harvest, no keeper of days before a day)

Rimfolk's world | a mission near its deadline with its goods not all there, a camp growing tense or hungry, a camp's question left waiting, a calendar day coming round, and one tomorrow with nothing laid by for it

Rooms, gently | a dining room with too few seats or too cramped, barracks that could become bedrooms, a hospital without what you've researched, a rec room with too little to do, a noble's bedroom short of the title, a kitchen with one stove for too many, a full freezer, a workshop with dark benches or no chairs, a prison cell without comfort

li.after: Defenses, power, fire risk, insects under the mountain, the dead, prisoners' needs and an idle research bench are watched too. Where a newer piece of advice says more, the older one steps aside: dark bedrooms and workshops have their own advice with lamps to plan, a mild winter's food has its own, and a calendar day tomorrow with nothing laid by replaces the plain reminder.

li.heading: When it speaks
li.text: A mission is pressing in its last two days, or its last quarter when that is under four. A decree is called costly only once what it was enacted for has passed (the food is no longer low, the threat is days gone) while more people are against it than for it and the moods add up to a loss of three or more. The winter advice comes within about twenty days of the cold, for a tribal or medieval colony, and only when the winter won't freeze the stores on its own. A kitchen has outgrown its stove at eight people with one stove, two cooks and fewer meals than mouths; a freezer is full when 17 of every 20 storage spots are taken while 30 or more pieces of food spoil outside it; a dining room is cramped when its space is rather tight or under two and a half for each of five or more.

li.heading: The plan: the colony's next steps
li.text: The Plan page (Colony, then Plan) keeps a short, ordered list of what to do next. Each hour the council proposes steps from what it watches: the priorities above, the defense advice and an idle research bench, at most eight at once, most pressing first. Take a step into the plan, or let it go (it isn't proposed again for a fortnight); add steps of your own, with a room plan if it's a room to build; move them up and down, or order the whole plan by urgency. Each step opens what does it: the room planner (at a suggested spot), the defense plan to place, the research to start, or the thing on the map. A step is done when you say so, or when the need behind it has passed for three hours running; done steps stay listed for five days. The first step shows on This week and in the council panel. "Ground plan" draws the plan's rooms and the proposals on the map together, each at the spot that fits best with the ones before it kept clear, with a button that opens the planner there. Switch the page off under "The colony's next steps".

li.heading: The base, looked over
li.text: The Base page (Colony, then Base) is the council's walk round the base, once an hour or when you ask. Rooms: a kitchen far from the freezer or the dining room, a workshop far from its store, a hospital far from the gate, a barn far from the fields; bedrooms or the hospital right by a workshop or a barn, a prison cell by the bedrooms. Walks: bedrooms a long way from the nearest dining room on average. Doors: a door with the same room on both sides or no wall beside it, and a freezer door that opens into a warm room or the open air with no airlock between. Walls: short stubs hanging off a proper wall that separate nothing (never a pillar on its own, a wall with a lamp on it, or one holding up a roof by itself). Conduits and pipes: runs that lead from a fork or a used piece to an end with nothing on it, conduit joined to nothing at all, and the same for Dubs Bad Hygiene's and Vanilla Expanded's pipes. Stores: stockpiles that take everything, goods lying about that no store accepts (with a button that lays out a stockpile for them by the store room), a bench far from the nearest store of its bills' materials (with a button that lays out a little store beside it, set to prefer them; never for raw food or corpses, which belong in the cold), one kind of goods accepted in three rooms or more, and stores whose filter allows nothing. Each finding says where to look; the doors, stubs, conduits and pipes have a button that gives the deconstruct orders, which you cancel on the map like any other. The findings are also proposed as steps on the Plan page.

li.heading: What you could make
li.text: The Making page (Colony, then Making) reads the recipes of every bench the colony has and checks them against the stock, so any mod's benches and recipes count by themselves. "You could make now" lists, bench by bench, each batch the stock allows that has no bill set for it and whose product the colony has fewer than sixty of, the staples first (meals, medicine, components, blocks, cloth) and of clothes and weapons only the dearest two; "Set a bill, until N" adds the bill to the bench, make until the colony has that many. "Harvests and finds nothing here uses" lists what the colony has a fair amount of that has a particular use at a bench the colony lacks (hops for a brewery, psychoid leaves for a drug lab, chunks for a stonecutter), the bench and the product, and the research it waits on, with a button to open it or to build the bench. Benches standing without bills are named at the bottom.
